assessment.title: CARSI Trauma & Biohazard Decontamination Practitioner — Practical task: plan and evidence a trauma decontamination job
assessment.instructions:
## Practical task

Plan and document a trauma and biohazard decontamination job from first call to client sign-off. Use a real job you have attended (with every identifying detail removed), or one of the supplied jobs:

- **Australia:** a ground-floor unit in Parramatta, NSW. A resident died and was found after several days. Police have released the scene and the property manager has instructed you. The bedroom is 3.2 m x 2.6 m with carpet on a concrete slab; the carpet stain is about 1.2 m x 0.9 m and a mattress is affected. A 10 A GPO in the hallway is available. Family members will be on site.
- **New Zealand:** a café kitchen in Christchurch after a staff injury. The owner has instructed you. About 1.5 m x 1.0 m of vinyl floor and a 0.6 m x 1.8 m timber bench are affected, and broken glass is present.

Keep everything non-graphic and respectful. Submit one PDF, or a set of photos and documents, containing:

1. **Release, authority and conduct.** Who released the scene and who instructed you, the law that applies (WHS Act, Victorian OHS Act or NZ HSWA), your low-profile arrival and how family, staff or neighbours are protected.
2. **Risk assessment and SWMS.** A site-specific hazard walk (biological, sharps, chemical, electrical, manual handling, heat, psychological), the control chosen for each from the top of the hierarchy down, the 230 V / RCD arrangement, and the stop-and-escalate triggers.
3. **PPE and exposure readiness.** The PPE set with the respirator standard (AS/NZS 1716) and fit-test record, the donning and doffing order, each worker's hepatitis B status (Australian or NZ Immunisation Handbook position), and the exposure response with the 72-hour PEP window and the AU or NZ numbers.
4. **Zones, removal and disinfection.** A zone sketch, the remove-or-clean decision for each material with reasons, areas in m², and the clean-then-disinfect record: product, ARTG number (AU) or label, SDS and supplier evidence (NZ), dilution in mL per litre, and contact time achieved.
5. **Sharps, waste and the job file.** Sharps handling and container, bag volumes (two-thirds rule), the waste rule for your jurisdiction (NSW, Victoria, another state's EPA, or NZS 4304 and the council), the crew wellbeing plan with support lines, the verification walk-through and the sign-off.

Write in Australian English, use metric units throughout, name standards only (no copied standard text), and price any quote in AUD (inc GST) or NZD for a NZ client.

criteria.label: Release, authority, law and conduct
criteria.description: Release and authority recorded with times; the correct law for the jurisdiction named; low-profile arrival; family, staff and neighbours protected; personal items and confidentiality handled respectfully and without graphic detail.

criteria.label: Risk assessment, SWMS and stop triggers
criteria.description: Every hazard class assessed; controls chosen from the top of the hierarchy down, consistent with the AU WHS principles or NZ GRWM regulation 6; 230 V gear through an RCD; the SWMS revised when the site changes; stop-and-escalate triggers stated.

criteria.label: PPE and exposure readiness
criteria.description: PPE matched to the remaining hazards; AS/NZS 1716 respirator with a fit test and fit check; a correct donning and doffing order; hepatitis B status recorded against the AU or NZ Handbook; the exposure response with 30-second wash, same-day assessment and the 72-hour PEP window; correct AU or NZ numbers.

criteria.label: Zones, removal and clean-then-disinfect
criteria.description: Three zones with one-way movement; real extent found beyond the visible edge; remove-or-clean decisions with reasons and m²; cleaning before disinfecting; dilution worked in mL per litre; contact time achieved; product claim checked on the ARTG (AU) or label, SDS and supplier evidence held (NZ).

criteria.label: Sharps, waste, crew wellbeing and the job file
criteria.description: Sharps found by looking and handled with tools into a rigid container closed at the fill line; bags at two-thirds or less with volumes; the correct jurisdiction waste rule and contractor; a crew wellbeing plan with support lines; a verification walk-through and client sign-off; Australian English, metric units, standards named only.
